sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COALESCE(t.cnt, 0) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) AS loc_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM lake.trips
    WHERE payment_type = 2
    GROUP BY CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT)
) t ON t.loc_id = z.LocationID
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query spends most time in the HASH_JOIN (node 8) and subsequent HASH_GROUP_BY because the join condition requires a runtime CAST from PULocationID (smallint) to BIGINT to match LocationID, preventing predicate pushdown and forcing a full scan of 99k filtered trips rows through the hash join before aggregation.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID condition in the HASH_JOIN prevents the payment_type=2 filter from being pushed into the trips scan as an index seek or partition prune, forcing a full sequential scan of the filtered 99k rows.

Because PULocationID has only 243 distinct values across 495k rows, the hash join builds a large hash table with many collisions on the right (zones) side, and the type coercion adds per-row CPU overhead during probing.
